Senses.Explanation: Literally, “great rest and great cessation.” The phrase occurs 93 times in 57 allowlisted texts. Chan records repeatedly call it a “secure field” or “field of great ease” (安穩之場; 大安樂田地), something one “reaches” or “personally arrives at” rather than an ordinary pause from activity. Yuanwu places it after “a great dead man has already lost his breath” and says, “upon reaching one’s own ground, great rest and great cessation” (到本分地上大休大歇). Xueyan immediately refuses to make that field an endpoint: “if you wish to head directly for the field of great rest, great cessation, and great ease, there is a great living road ahead” (前頭大有活路在). A later master criticizes descendants who bite onto Linji’s four shouts and take that for the field of great rest and cessation, calling the identification “a sheep’s substance in a tiger’s hide” (羊質虎皮). The Chan deviation is therefore an explicitly named field of arrival that remains subject to public correction; the entry reports those predicates without defining an inner state.
Senses.Note: The corpus’s place nouns are metaphors for the same named condition, not distinct referents. A late record itself names it “the sea of great extinction,” “the ground of actuality,” and “the idle person of no learning and no contrivance” (大寂滅海; 實際理地; 絕學無為閑道人); these are that text’s names, not this entry’s imported definition.

Occurrences.Kwic: 透到大休大歇安穩之場，豈有二致哉？
似大死人已絕氣息。到本分地上大休大歇。
若欲直趣大休大歇大安樂田地，前頭大有活路在。
致令後代兒孫咬住矢橛，以為大休大歇的田地。正眼看來，大似羊質虎皮。
大休大歇，乃佛祖力行親到之處，謂之大寂滅海，謂之實際理地，謂之絕學無為閑道人

AlternateTargets: a person of great thorough awakening
Senses.Explanation: Literally, "greatly penetrate and greatly awaken": great thorough awakening. The phrase occurs 48 times in 30 allowlisted texts. It names an event or resulting qualification in biographies, appraisals, and questions. One record says that people of great thorough awakening have finished the matter of inquiry and afterward stayed by water and woods until pushed forward to address others (古人大徹大悟，參學事畢，且於水邊林下). A public exchange tests the qualification directly: one master says there is nobody of great thorough awakening in the hall; another asks, "which one is not of great thorough awakening?" and the first counters, "which one is?" (那箇不是大徹大悟的；那箇是大徹大悟的). A Dahui record places it beside "the mind-ground opens and passes through" (大徹大悟，心地開通) and calls Zhaozhou's dog public case a key that opens that mind-ground. A later address jokes that its third phrase could make people greatly and thoroughly awaken, then refuses to utter it because nobody would remain to watch the Chan hall. These records attest the phrase as event, qualification, question, and comic hall claim; this entry adds no meaning beyond those recorded deployments.
Senses.Note: Eventive and attributive grammar concern the same awakening, not different referents: “to awaken thoroughly” and “a thoroughly awakened person” remain one sense. The phrase is related to, but lexically stronger than, “great awakening” (大悟); this entry does not infer a graded awakening system absent an explicit passage.

Occurrences.Kwic: 古人大徹大悟，參學事畢，且於水邊林下長養聖胎，不惜口頭生醭，龍天推出，方乃為人。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The passage says ancient people of great thorough awakening had finished inquiry and stayed by water and woods until pushed forward to address others.

Occurrences.Kwic: 柱云：「好一堂師僧，沒箇大徹大悟的。」師云：「瞎漢！那箇不是大徹大悟的？」柱云：「瞎漢！那箇是大徹大悟的？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Two masters publicly counter-question whether anyone—or everyone—in the hall qualifies as greatly and thoroughly awakened.

Occurrences.Kwic: 也要得透脫生死，除非大徹大悟，心地開通。僧問趙州：狗子還有佛性也無？州云：無。此箇公案，正是開大徹大悟心地底鑰匙子也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The passage pairs great thorough awakening with the mind-ground opening and calls Zhaozhou's dog public case a key opening that ground.

Occurrences.Kwic: 第三句能令人大徹大悟，不敢舉，恐汝等皆大徹大悟，打筋斗去了，叫那箇守這禪堂？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A hall address says the third phrase could cause great thorough awakening, then jokingly withholds it lest everyone somersault away and leave the hall unattended.

Senses.Explanation: (大) great / thorough + (悟) to wake up, to realize. The decisive, complete breakthrough, set against (小悟) (small, partial awakenings). Overwhelmingly a verb of the breakthrough moment: (於言下大悟) 'was greatly awakened at [these] words' — the classic form being Linji under Dayu (師於言下大悟…元來黃檗佛法無多子, 'was greatly awakened and said: so there isn't much to Huangbo's Buddha's teaching after all'). The fixed noun phrase (大悟底人) 'a greatly-awakened person' names one who has had it. It is waking up thoroughly. The case (大悟底人為甚麼卻迷) ('the greatly-awakened person, why do they fall back into delusion?') pairs (大悟) with (迷) (delusion), answered (破鏡不重照)，(落花難上枝) ('a broken mirror does not shine again; fallen blossoms do not climb back onto the branch'). Allowlist grep counts fix the breakthrough-verb profile: 2,711 hits in 308 of 462 texts; (言下大悟) 446 (師於言下大悟 151), (豁然大悟) 353, (忽然大悟) 205, (大徹大悟) 41, (遂大悟) 37, against (小悟) 58. The (迷) case's oldest lamp witness is the Zutang-ji, with archaic (什摩): (問)：「(大悟底人為什摩卻迷)？」(師云)：「(破鏡不重照)，(落花難上枝)。」 (B25n0144), and the (大悟底人) family (16 hits in 14 texts) extends to other test-questions: (僧問)：「(大悟底人還有憎愛也無)？」(師云)：「(能愛人)，(能惡人)。」 ('does the greatly-awakened person still have hatred and love? — He can love people, and can hate people', J10nA158). The record also carries the word in Yongjia's (證道歌) maxim (大象不遊於兔徑)。(大悟不拘於小節) ('the great elephant does not travel the rabbit's path; great awakening is not bound by small details', T48n2014; 大悟不拘於小節 13 hits, quoted e.g. as 故永嘉亦云。大悟不拘於小節, B25n0145), and as the stock question (如何是大悟無道) (大悟無道 22 hits), in several records asked in series with (如何是大富無糧) and answered divergently: (貧恨一身多) (J28nB220), (莫妄想) (X82n1571), (賊) (X68n1319). Dahui's record ties (悟) to doubt: (今時學道者多不自疑)。(却疑他人)。(所以道)。(大疑之下必有大悟) ('students today mostly do not doubt themselves — they doubt others; hence the saying: under great doubt there is necessarily great awakening', T47n1998A; 大疑大悟 33 hits in 28 texts).
Senses.Note: The famous self-report (大悟十八遍)，(小悟不計數) ('eighteen great awakenings, countless small ones'), popularly credited to Dahui Zonggao, is explicitly flagged in the Zen record (J10nA158) as (本是宋儒言)，(非大慧所說) — 'actually a Song-Confucian's phrase, NOT spoken by Dahui.' Do NOT credit the eighteen-awakenings line to Dahui as authentic. The base word (大悟) is itself rock-solid multi-source; only this quantified self-report's Dahui-attribution is disputed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師於言下大悟云。元來黃檗佛法無多子。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (景德傳燈錄), (臨濟義玄) section: (師) = Linji, awakened at Dayu's words after Huangbo's blows. The verbal-breakthrough use (於言下大悟).

Occurrences.Kwic: 大悟底人為甚麼却迷。師曰。破鏡不重照。落花難上枝。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (五燈會元): (師) = (華嚴休靜) (Huayan Xiujing), disciple of Dongshan; the preceding narrative has (後唐莊宗) summoning him to the capital. The (大悟底人卻迷) dialectic.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉僧問華嚴：「大悟底人為甚麼卻迷？」嚴云：「破鏡不重照，落花難上枝。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Independent (頌古) witness citing the case (舉): a monk asks, (華嚴) (嚴云) answers. MasterName null because this KWIC is a two-speaker quoted case citation, not a single-speaker saying; it corroborates the X80 Huayan attribution of the case (names 華嚴/嚴 as the answering master).

Occurrences.Kwic: 大悟十八遍，小悟不計數，本是宋儒言，非大慧所說。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Verse-annotation flagging the '18 great awakenings' line as a misattribution to Dahui (非大慧所說). Cited for the attribution caveat, NOT as Dahui's words.

AlternateTargets: the great trigger and the great use
Senses.Explanation: The components mean “great” (大), “pivot, trigger, loom-mechanism, or latent capacity” (機), “great” again (大), and “function, activity, or use” (用): 'great capacity, great function.' The corpus itself splits the compound into (大機) and (大用) and assigns each to a master: in (仰山慧寂)'s (語錄), (溈山) asks about (百丈)'s second visit to (馬祖) (raising the whisk) and (仰山) answers '(此是顯大機大用)'; to '(幾人得大機)？(幾人得大用)？' he answers '(百丈得大機)，(黃檗得大用)，(餘者盡是唱導之師)' — the same dialogue recurs in (古尊宿語錄) and elsewhere. It is split further into (大機之用) (72× in 43 files) and (大用之機) (13× in 10): '(如何是大機大用)？(如何是大機之用)？(如何是大用之機)？' (posed in 天隱圓修's record). It names what (黃檗) said he saw in (馬祖): '(見馬祖大機大用然且不識馬祖)'. In expanded couplet form it runs '(大機圓應大用縱橫)' (圜悟克勤) and '(大機圓應大用直截)' (1×, 禪宗頌古聯珠通集 C078n1720) (大機圓應 16× in 12 files; 全機大用 115×; 大用現前 447×). It is also a term masters warn against misusing: '(以麄放狂亂為大機大用)' (玉林通琇, 客問) and '(觸著則任意揮張)，(便道大機大用)…(可見大機大用不在蒲團禪板上)' (天隱圓修). (大機大用) occurs 276× in 124 allowlist files. The texts deploy it as praise of a master's activity, as a test-question split into (機) and (用), and as a target of caution, without assigning it a gloss beyond the literal, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: The compound's own structure is set by the corpus, not by the annotator: (大機) (988× in 245 files) and (大用) (2094× in 330) are the two halves, and the stock (溈山)–(仰山) dialogue distributes them — (百丈得大機)、(黃檗得大用) — the line (百丈得大機) recurring in 23 allowlist files, incl. (仰山慧寂語錄) (T47n1990), (古尊宿語錄) (C077n1710), (五燈會元) (X80n1565), (續傳燈錄) (T51n2077), (從容庵錄) (T48n2004), and (禪宗頌古聯珠通集) (C078n1720). Do NOT read the split as this entry's interpretation; it is the texts'. Three attested deployments: (1) praise / description of a master's activity (黃檗 seeing 馬祖's 大機大用; the 圓應…縱橫 / 直截 couplet); (2) a test-question further split into (大機之用) / (大用之機); (3) an error masters name and warn against (以麄放狂亂為大機大用; 大機大用不在蒲團禪板上). Roster witnesses across houses: (仰山慧寂), (圜悟克勤) (Linji line), (天隱圓修), (玉林通琇). The (溈山)–(仰山) exchange is a two-speaker dialogue and the (黃檗)/(馬祖) line is (黃檗)'s reported speech inside (百丈)'s section, so those are left unattributed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 百丈得大機，黃檗得大用，餘者盡是唱導之師。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (袁州仰山慧寂禪師語錄) (T47n1990). The line is (仰山慧寂)'s own answer ('師云') to (溈山)'s '(幾人得大機)？(幾人得大用)？', inside (仰山)'s (語錄) — but it is a two-speaker (溈山問仰山) dialogue, so MasterName null per the raised/dialogue rule. This is the defining locus that splits (大機大用) into (大機) (百丈) and (大用) (黃檗).

Occurrences.Kwic: 百丈得大機黃檗得大用餘者盡是唱道之師
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (古尊宿語錄), (百丈懷海禪師語錄) section; the same (溈山問仰山) dialogue ('此是顯大機大用…幾人得大機幾人得大用…百丈得大機黃檗得大用'), an independent witness. Raised dialogue → null. C-canon unpunctuated (verbatim); note (唱道) here vs (唱導) in T47n1990.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何是大機大用？如何是大機之用？如何是大用之機？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (天隱和尚語錄) (天隱圓修). The assembly's (問) ('古人道：一人得大機，一人得大用') driving toward (師答) — a two-speaker test-question, so MasterName null. Attests the further split into (大機之用) and (大用之機).

Occurrences.Kwic: 見馬祖大機大用然且不識馬祖
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (古尊宿語錄), (百丈懷海禪師語錄) section; the stock case where (黃檗) (檗曰) tells (百丈) he 'saw (馬祖)'s (大機大用) yet did not know (馬祖)'. Reported speech of (黃檗) inside (百丈)'s record, two-speaker → null. Attests the term as praise/description of a master's activity.

Occurrences.Kwic: 可見大機大用不在蒲團禪板上。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (天隱和尚語錄) (天隱圓修), own critique of false teachers: '(觸著則任意揮張)，(便道大機大用)…(學人問著蒲團)，(即將蒲團打)…(若將不得)，(可見大機大用不在蒲團禪板上)'. Own words. The term as a named error.

Occurrences.Kwic: 以麄放狂亂為大機大用
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (普濟玉琳國師語錄) (玉林通琇), (客問) (cb:mulu: 客問評註) — in the master's reply to the (客), under (第三須悟處諦當), a list of mistakes: '(以鹵莾承當為有力量)…(以麄放狂亂為大機大用以顢頇為透脫無餘)'. The answering voice is (玉林)'s own; second independent witness of the term deployed as a warning. B-canon unpunctuated (verbatim).

Occurrences.Kwic: 大機圓應大用縱橫。不墮千聖機關。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (圓悟佛果禪師語錄) (= 圜悟克勤; roster spelling 圜悟克勤), '(師云)。(大機圓應大用縱橫)…(舉一機千機截斷)。(拈一事萬事齊彰)'. Own words; the expanded couplet form (大機圓應 / 大用縱橫).

Senses.Explanation: (大) great + (死) death / to die: 'the great death.' The corpus glosses the term in its own words. Yuanwu (圜悟) on the type: (大死底人)。(都無佛法道理玄妙得失是非長短) — the greatly-dead person has no Buddha's teaching, no stated principle, no mystery, no gain-and-loss, no right-and-wrong, no long-and-short; in the same Blue Cliff Record (碧巖錄) commentary he reports his teacher's wording — (五祖先師)。(謂之命根不斷)。(須是大死一番)。(却活始得) ('Wuzu, my late master, called it [having anything to lean on or any interpretation] the life-root not yet cut: one must die the great death once; only coming back to life will do'). Two idioms carry it. (1) (大死一番), 'die the great death once' (22 hits / 16 files): (直須絕名利)、(忘人我)，(大死一番方堪湊泊) ('you must cut off name-and-gain, forget self-and-other, and die the great death once — only then can you moor'; the recorded sayings of Chan Master Baiyu, 百愚禪師語錄), (秪管大死一番)，(不怕不活) ('just die the great death once — no fear you will not come back to life'; the recorded sayings of Chan Master Miyun, 密雲禪師語錄), and alongside it the stock verse (絕後再甦)。(欺君不得) ('revived after utter cutoff — he cannot be cheated'; 3 verbatim hits, 絕後再甦 alone 222 hits / 119 files, also written 絕後再蘇, 34 / 22). (2) (大死底人), 'the person who has died the great death' (99 hits / 58 files), which stands almost always inside the Zhaozhou–Touzi question — (大死底人) followed by (却)/(卻活時如何) ('when he comes back to life, what then?') in 74 of the 99 hits: (州問)。(大死底人)。(却活時如何) ('Zhou asked: the person who has died the great death — when he comes back to life, what then?') → Touzi answers (不許夜行)。(投明須到) ('no travelling by night; you must arrive by daylight'); the exact second clause (投明須到) recurs 192 times in 104 files. The compound (大死大活) ('greatly die, greatly live') is attested but rare (4 hits / 2 files). In Dahui's (大慧) letter (示東峯居士) ('shown to the layman Dongfeng') the phrase appears in a chain of appellations: (喚作默而常照)。(又喚作如大死底人)。(又喚作父母未生時事)。(又喚作空劫已前事) ('it is called "silent yet constantly shining"; also called "like a person who has died the great death"; also called "the matter before father and mother were born"; also called "the matter before the empty eon"'). One late imperial anthology's general preface gives a source-specific equivalence: 'this is called passing the heavy barrier; it is called one who greatly dies and greatly lives' (是則名為透重關，名為大死大活者). The explicit equation with 'passing the heavy barrier' (透重關) is a single late explanatory witness and remains provisional within the broader corpus-wide entry.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide sense; the (大死底人) ('person who has died the great death') case (Zhaozhou–Touzi) and the (大死一番) ('die the great death once') exhortation are two forms of the same term, and both are attested with revival wording alongside (却活時如何 'when he comes back to life, what then?' / 却活始得 'only coming back to life will do' / 不怕不活 'no fear you will not come back to life' / 絕後再甦 'revived after utter cutoff'). Multi-source across independent records (the 五燈會元 Compendium of the Five Lamps / the 碧巖錄 Blue Cliff Record / Dahui's recorded sayings 大慧語錄). Raw grep: (大死) 343 hits / 132 allowlist files (tag-stripped, 2026-07-11).

Occurrences.Kwic: 州問。大死底人。却活時如何。師曰。不許夜行。投明須到。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (五燈會元), mulu head (舒州投子山大同禪師) (Touzi's section). The KWIC is an explicit two-speaker exchange — (州問) (Zhaozhou asks) … (師曰) (Touzi answers) — so MasterName is null per the two-speaker rule. The defining answer (不許夜行投明須到) is Touzi Datong's (Touzi is retained in RelatedMasters); the corpus-wide sense's multi-source status holds independently via (大慧) / (圜悟) / (柏山楷).

Occurrences.Kwic: 大死底人。都無佛法道理玄妙得失是非長短。到這裏只恁麼休去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (碧巖錄) case 41 (圜悟 commentary on the Zhaozhou–Touzi case); (圜悟)'s in-commentary gloss of the term. Raised-case commentary → null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 喚作默而常照。又喚作如大死底人。又喚作父母未生時事。又喚作空劫已前事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (大慧普覺禪師語錄), (示東峯居士); Dahui's own letter — (如大死底人) stands in his chain of appellations (喚作…又喚作…).

Occurrences.Kwic: 欲學斯道，必須大死一番始得。古德曰：「死盡偷心，方堪入室。絕後再甦，欺君不得。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (柏山楷禪師語錄), (與太谷眾居士) (his own letter; master not in the roster). Shows (大死一番) alongside the stock (絕後再甦) verse.

Occurrences.Kwic: 是則名為透重關，名為大死大活者。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The imperial general preface to the Selected Recorded Sayings (御選語錄) says, 'this is called passing the heavy barrier; it is called one who greatly dies and greatly lives' (是則名為透重關，名為大死大活者). This is a late preface's explicit equivalence, not the older Zhaozhou–Touzi case.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, great (大) function or use (用): "great function." The term occurs 2,094 times in 330 allowlisted texts. Its dominant formula is "great function manifests before you" (大用現前, 447 occurrences in 170 texts), frequently followed by "it does not preserve rules" (不存軌則). In one public interview a monk asks what it is like when great function manifests without preserving rules; the answer is, "if you can use it, then use it" (汝用得但用), after which the monk bares his shoulder and is struck. Another asks separately, "what is great capacity?" and "what is great function?" and receives a blow across the back for each. The corpus coordinates "great function" with "great capacity" (大機大用, 276 occurrences), and "great function" with "the whole capacity" (全機大用, 115). It also records the explicit contrast "you people have obtained only the great body, not great function" (汝等諸人只得大體不得大用). These are named formulas, questions, pairings, and contrasts in the record; the entry makes no claim about a metaphysical entity behind them.
Senses.Note: No distinct referent emerged from 'great function' (大用), 'great function manifests before you' (大用現前), 'great capacity and great function' (大機大用), 'the whole capacity and great function' (全機大用), and the 'great body/great function' (大體/大用) comparison. 'Use' and 'function' are alternate English readings of the same attested thing, not separate senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。大用現前．不存軌則時如何。師曰。汝用得但用。僧乃脫膊。遶師三匝。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A public interview asks about the fixed formula; the reply repeats the graph for 'use' (用), and the encounter proceeds to an action.

Occurrences.Kwic: 夫參學眼目。臨機直須大用現前。莫自拘於小節。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Records of the Human and Heavenly Eye preserve Fengxue's instruction linking the formula to meeting the occasion and not binding oneself to minor details.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：「如何是大機？」師劈脊便打。進云：「如何是大用？」師劈脊便打。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A late public interview distinguishes the questions 'what is great capacity?' and 'what is great function?'; each receives a blow.

Occurrences.Kwic: 溈山上堂云汝等諸人只得大體不得大用師抽身出去溈山召之師更不迴顧
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An early lamp fragment preserves Guishan's explicit great-body/great-function contrast and the student's departure.

Occurrences.Kwic: 溈山云馬祖出八十四人善知識幾人得大機幾人得大用仰山云百丈得大機黃檗得大用

Senses.Explanation: Literally, “great function appears before one”: “great” (大), “functioning or use” (用), and “appears before one or is manifest” (現前). The phrase occurs 447 times in 170 allowlisted texts. It is frequently followed by “does not retain rules” (不存軌則); the unpunctuated five-character continuation occurs 21 times in 12 texts. The records deploy the headword as an assertion, a question, and a line in an address. In an early collected discourse, the statement “great function appearing is the unequalled body of the teaching” (大用現前即是無等等法身) directly equates it with another named expression. Asked, “When great function appears and does not retain rules, what then?”, Changqing Da'an says, “If you can use it, just use it” (汝用得但用). Yunmen states the stock line, receives the question “What is great function appearing?”, raises his staff, and calls out, “Old man Shakyamuni has come!” (釋迦老子來也). Fengxue Yanzhao tells the assembly that at the encounter they must have great function appear and not constrain themselves to small details. Yuanwu Keqin’s case commentary pairs the stock line with using a blade of grass as a sixteen-foot golden body and using a sixteen-foot golden body as a blade of grass. Dahui Zonggao supplies an explicit corrective witness: students of sayings call Guizong’s killing a snake and Nanquan’s killing a cat “timely wondrous function” and also “great function appears, not retaining rules,” but Dahui says that is not the account. The correction prevents those two cases from being made definitions of the headword.
Senses.Note: The question “What is great function appearing?” (如何是大用現前) occurs 22 times in 19 texts, and the exact collocation “at the encounter, great function appears” (臨機大用現前) occurs twice in two. The corpus supplies many different replies and actions; the entry reports representative deployment shapes and Dahui’s explicit rejection without assigning a single hidden force to them.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, ‘great doubt.’ The phrase occurs 196 times in 91 allowlisted texts. A direct definition says, ‘doubt has no large or small; only when the doubt is weighty is it called great doubt, and when light it is called small doubt’ (疑情無大小，但疑之重，是謂大疑；疑之輕，是謂小疑). The same record says that when one cannot refrain from raising it, ‘therefore it is named great doubt.’ Across other texts it appears in the fixed contrast ‘great doubt, great awakening; small doubt, small awakening; no doubt, no awakening,’ in questions about ‘a person of great doubt,’ and in biographies where a master ‘greatly doubted’ after an exchange or saying. Thus the corpus uses the phrase both as a named weight of doubt and verbally for becoming deeply doubtful; English ‘great doubt’ covers both without positing different referents.
Senses.Note: Zen bends an ordinary degree phrase by making it a named category explicitly defined against small doubt and repeatedly paired with great awakening. The family comparison with ‘doubt-mass’ (疑情) and ‘ball of doubt’ (疑團) supports one sense, not a noun/verb split: both constructions name the same doubt.
